messages.subject: Re: Java Issue??
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Maybe try setting memory.limit higher..
Check how much is currently allocated with memory.limit()
Check how much is currently in use with memory.size()

To change the maximum memory limit you could do it two ways.
1.
In JGR use:
memory.limit(4096)
to allocate 4096 (~4Gb) to Java.

2.
To have it always allocate more ram, in Rprofile.site add something like..

utils::memory.limit(10240)

this would allocate 10240mb to Java on startup.

Of course, you can't allocate anything higher than the amount of system ram you have..

good luck.

messages.body_plain:

Noting strange results in the preview window of a run of the logistic model I decided to follow Ian Fellows video about the topic and with the birthwt data and it has the same problem. That is the default option ANOVA table gives an error message
"Error in `colnames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("Df", "Chisq", "Pr(>Chisq)", :
  length of 'dimnames' [2] not equal to array extent"

because of which, I understand, there is no ANOVA table to be seen in the preview box or in the final result and the preview box does not present itself formated as it should be but completely unformated as:

    >Anova(.gui.working.env$model.glm,type='II',test.statistic='Wald')

    as.factor(race) + as.factor(smoke), family = binomial(), data =

    Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|) (Intercept) -0.5517 0.1833 -3.009 0.00262 **
    as.factor(race)1 -0.7309 0.2490 -2.936 0.00333 ** as.factor(race)2 0.3532
    0.2992 1.181 0.23776 as.factor(smoke)1 -0.5580 0.1846 -3.023 0.00251 **
    --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
    (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1) Null deviance:

Thanks for the support in fixing this error. It will be greatly appreciated

Jose Ferreira

messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for the idea, but unfortunately, changing the application compatibility settings did not fix it.  In checking to see if it resolved the issue, I noticed this is also an issue with the base R - there are just so many fewer dialogue boxes that it goes unnoticed.  It appears to be some kind of screen scaling issue so your idea may be on the right track.  Lowering screen resolution just made everything quite a bit smaller.  :(  It is a much bigger issue in Deducer, where the plot builder ends up extremely small and dialogue boxes become unreadable sometimes.

Does anyone else have any ideas?

On Friday, January 30, 2015 at 1:55:01 PM UTC-5, Tom wrote:
> This might be a problem with high-DPI screens and software that doesn't correctly inherit the scaling from Windows (probably a problem in the Java libraries used by Deduce).

> http://kynosarges.org/WindowsDpi.html%23OptOut
